author: Anonymous (Asia)
occasion: No occasion or purpose is stated in the text. It records Decius's decree, Maximus's voluntary appearance, interrogation, torture, sentence and stoning.
argument: Emperor Decius ordered Christians throughout the world to leave the living and true God, sacrifice to demons, or face punishment. Maximus, a freeborn commoner who lives by his own business, presented himself voluntarily in Asia and confessed to the proconsul Optimus that he is a Christian and servant of Christ. He rejects the imperial order as unjust, refuses to sacrifice to any but God, and says he seeks to exchange miserable temporal life for eternal life. Under beating and the rack he reframes his sufferings as anointings, sustained by Christ's grace and the example of fellow contenders, and says true loss is sacrificing and losing one's soul. Condemned for refusing to sacrifice to Diana, he gives thanks to God the Father through Jesus Christ as he is seized, is led outside the walls and struck with stones until he dies, and the narrator closes with a doxology to Christ.

outline.move: Decius's universal sacrifice decree is given, Maximus presents himself in Asia, and Optimus interrogates him about name, status, trade, Christianity, and the decree, ending in Maximus's refusal to sacrifice.
Maximus is beaten and racked while disputing with Optimus over sacrifice, soul, suffering, and grace, and Optimus condemns him to be stoned for refusing Diana as a warning to other Christians.

Maximus gives thanks to God the Father through Jesus Christ as he is seized and carried off, is then led outside the walls, struck with stones, and dies, and the narrator gives the place, day, persecutors, and closing doxology to Christ.

scripture: No biblical book is named, quoted, or numbered in this text, so no LXX/Vulgate naming or Psalm-numbering habit can be established; general mentions of God, Christ, and the gospel should be rendered with standard modern book names and modern chapter-verse citations if parallels are noted.
uncertain: Date and place of composition are not given; c. 250 CE is the dramatic date under Decius, not an established date of writing.
Whether the narrative records a historical event, and the identity and office of the proconsul Optimus, cannot be established from the text alone.
The exact city in Asia and the meaning of the date formula secundo idus Maii beyond May 14 cannot be established from the text alone.

_unresolved_facts.claim: No occasion or purpose is stated in the text.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Decius imperator volens opprimere vel superare legem Christianorum, decreta constituit per universum orbem
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text does state an occasion. Decius wants to suppress or overcome the Christian law, so he issues a decree that all Christians sacrifice to demons or be punished. No authorial purpose or addressee is given.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Optimus interrogates him about name, status, trade, Christianity, and the decree, ending in Maximus's refusal to sacrifice.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Hoc est quod semper optavi. propterea enim me manifestavi, ut tandem carens miserabili et temporali vita aeternam reciperem.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Section 1 refuses sacrifice earlier ("Ego non sacrifico nisi soli deo"). It ends after Optimus's threat of varied torments, with Maximus saying he has always wished for this and came forward to gain eternal life.

Add rendering notes for the names in the text: Decius (Decius), Optimus (Optimus), Maximus (Maximus), Asia (the Roman province, "apud Asiam provinciam"), Diana ("the great goddess Diana"), Iesus Christus (Jesus Christ).
